# anovakit

anovakit has eight analysis-of-variance functions: Welch’s ANOVA,
Kruskal-Wallis, ANCOVA, repeated measures, MANOVA, and analyses of
deviance for binary, count and other GLM outcomes. They take the same
arguments and return the same kind of object. Each one checks the
assumptions its method needs, reports effect sizes, marginal means and
pairwise comparisons, builds `ggplot2` figures without drawing them, and
records in `$notes` every decision it made for you.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("elkronos/anovakit", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

`install_github()` skips vignettes unless you pass
`build_vignettes = TRUE`, so without it
[`vignette("anovakit")`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/anovakit.md)
is not available.

## Which function

| Function | Response | Use it when |
|----|----|----|
| [`anova_welch()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_welch.md) | one numeric | Comparing means. The default choice: it does not assume equal variances. |
| [`anova_kw()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_kw.md) | one numeric | No distributional assumption. Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn post-hoc. Convert an ordered factor with [`as.integer()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/integer.html) first. |
| [`anova_ancova()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_ancova.md) | one numeric | Adjusting for one or more numeric covariates. |
| [`anova_rm()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_rm.md) | one numeric | The same subjects measured repeatedly. |
| [`anova_manova()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_manova.md) | two or more numeric | Several outcomes analysed jointly, with or without covariates. |
| [`anova_bin()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_bin.md) | binary | Logistic regression, odds ratios, marginal probabilities. |
| [`anova_count()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_count.md) | counts | Poisson, quasi-Poisson or negative binomial, with exposure offsets. |
| [`anova_glm()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_glm.md) | anything | A classical factorial ANOVA with main effects and interactions, Type II or III (the default Gaussian family), or any other GLM family. |

Six take `data, response, groups`, with columns named as character
strings.
[`anova_manova()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_manova.md)
takes `responses` (plural), and
[`anova_rm()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_rm.md)
takes `response` with `subject`, `within` and `between`. [Choose an
analysis](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/choosing.html)
walks through the choice.

## A first example

Fuel economy of 32 cars, by number of cylinders:

``` r

library(anovakit)

fit <- anova_welch(mtcars, "mpg", "cyl")
fit
#> Welch's analysis of variance 
#> ----------------------------
#> Call: anova_welch(data = mtcars, response = "mpg", groups = "cyl")
#> Observations used: 32
#> 
#> Omnibus test (Welch F)
#>   term statistic num_df den_df   p_value
#> 1  cyl     31.62      2  18.03 1.271e-06
#> 
#> Notes
#>   - Largest group variance is 9.63 times the smallest. Welch's test handles this; the classical F test would not.
#> 
#> Plots available: means, box, qq
#>   (use plot(x, which = "means"))

fit$posthoc[, c("group1", "group2", "difference", "conf_low", "conf_high", "p_adjusted")]
#>   group1 group2 difference conf_low conf_high   p_adjusted
#> 1      4      6   6.920779 3.751376 10.090182 4.048495e-04
#> 2      4      8  11.563636 8.318518 14.808755 4.924043e-06
#> 3      6      8   4.642857 2.802925  6.482789 9.080709e-05

summary(fit)       # adds the assumption checks, effect sizes and group summaries
plot(fit, "means") # a ggplot2 object
```

The comparisons are Welch t tests with Holm-adjusted p-values. `cyl` is
numeric in `mtcars`; grouping columns are converted to factors.

## What you get

- The omnibus test in `$anova`, with the sums of squares, statistic and
  any correction named in the printed heading.
- Effect sizes in `$effect_sizes`, with intervals for standardised mean
  differences, odds ratios and rate ratios.
- Marginal means in `$emmeans` and pairwise comparisons in `$posthoc`,
  with both the unadjusted and the adjusted p-value.
- The assumption checks that fit the method in `$assumptions`.
- `ggplot2` objects in `$plots`, returned and never drawn.
- One `conf_level` for every interval, and no console output from any
  analysis function.
- `$notes`: dropped rows, centred covariates, a switch from Poisson to
  negative binomial, a perfectly separated cell.

## Documentation

The website, <https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/>, has:

- [Get
  started](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/anovakit.html):
  one analysis from start to finish, and the arguments every function
  shares.
- [Choose an
  analysis](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/choosing.html):
  four questions that lead to one of the eight functions.
- [Walkthroughs and
  guides](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/index.html): one
  worked analysis per function, and guides to results, diagnostics,
  plots, weights and the design choices behind the defaults.
- The [function
  reference](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/index.html).

From R:

``` r

vignette("anovakit")      # Get started
?anova_welch              # any function
?anovakit_fit             # what the returned object holds
citation("anovakit")
```

Report bugs and request features at
<https://github.com/elkronos/anovakit/issues>.

## Dependencies

Imports `car`, `emmeans`, `ggplot2` (3.4.0 or later) and base R.

`afex` (repeated measures), `MASS` (negative binomial) and `sandwich`
(robust standard errors) are Suggests. Without `afex`,
[`anova_rm()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_rm.md)
stops with a message, as does `anova_count(model = "negbin")` without
`MASS`. Where a fallback exists, the function uses it and says so in
`$notes`: `model = "auto"` without `MASS` fits quasi-Poisson where it
would have chosen the negative binomial, and `vcov_type` without
`sandwich` uses model-based standard errors. `bit64` is needed only to
read `integer64` columns.

Dunn’s test, Mardia’s tests, Box’s M and the canonical discriminant
analysis are implemented in the package rather than imported.

## Licence

GPL-3.

# Package index

## Analysis functions

Each takes a data frame and column names given as character strings, and
returns an `anovakit_fit`.

### Continuous outcomes

- [`anova_welch()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_welch.md)
  : Welch's Analysis of Variance
- [`anova_kw()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_kw.md)
  : Kruskal-Wallis Test with Dunn Post-hoc Comparisons
- [`anova_ancova()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_ancova.md)
  : Analysis of Covariance
- [`anova_rm()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_rm.md)
  : Repeated Measures Analysis of Variance
- [`anova_manova()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_manova.md)
  : Multivariate Analysis of Variance and Covariance

### Binary, count and other outcomes

- [`anova_bin()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_bin.md)
  : Analysis of Deviance for a Binary Response
- [`anova_count()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_count.md)
  : Analysis of Deviance for a Count Response
- [`anova_glm()`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anova_glm.md)
  : Analysis of Deviance for a Generalised Linear Model

## The fitted object

What every function returns, and the methods for it.

- [`anovakit_fit`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anovakit_fit.md)
  : The object returned by every anovakit function
- [`print(`*`<anovakit_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/print.anovakit_fit.md)
  : Print an anovakit result
- [`summary(`*`<anovakit_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/summary.anovakit_fit.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.anovakit_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/summary.anovakit_fit.md)
  : Summarise an anovakit result
- [`plot(`*`<anovakit_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/plot.anovakit_fit.md)
  : Plot an anovakit result

## Package overview

- [`anovakit`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anovakit-package.md)
  [`anovakit-package`](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/reference/anovakit-package.md)
  : anovakit: Analysis of Variance Workflows

# Articles

### Start here

- [Get started with
  anovakit](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/anovakit.md):

  One analysis from start to finish (Welch’s ANOVA on mtcars, then the
  same question with a covariate in anova_ancova()), and the arguments
  every function shares.

- [Choose an
  analysis](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/choosing.md):

  A decision guide: four questions about your data that lead to one of
  the eight functions, a table of common situations, and what each
  function is for.

### One outcome, independent groups

- [Welch's ANOVA: comparing means when variances
  differ](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/welch.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_welch(): the omnibus Welch test, pairwise Welch
  t tests, standardised mean differences that do not assume equal
  variances, and the three diagnostic plots.

- [Kruskal-Wallis: comparing groups by
  ranks](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/kruskal-wallis.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_kw(): the Kruskal-Wallis test, epsilon squared,
  Dunn’s comparisons with the tie correction, missing and infinite
  values, and the optional diagnostics.

- [ANCOVA: comparing groups at the same value of a
  covariate](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/ancova.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_ancova() on the anorexia treatment data: the
  homogeneity-of-slopes test, simple slopes, covariate centring,
  adjusted marginal means and robust standard errors (vcov_type).

### Repeated measures and several outcomes

- [Repeated measures ANOVA: the same subjects under several
  conditions](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/repeated-measures.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_rm(): mixed designs, sphericity corrections,
  generalised eta squared, within-subject residual checks, incomplete
  subjects and repeated rows.

- [MANOVA: comparing groups on several responses at
  once](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/manova.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_manova() on the iris measurements: the
  multivariate test, univariate follow-ups, canonical discriminant
  analysis, Box’s M and Mardia’s tests, MANCOVA and several grouping
  variables.

### Binary, count and other outcomes

- [Binary outcomes: logistic regression with
  anova_bin()](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/binary.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_bin() on the Berkeley admissions data: analysis
  of deviance, odds ratios, marginal probabilities, separation,
  frequency weights and robust standard errors.

- [Counts and rates: analysis of deviance with
  anova_count()](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/counts.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_count() on the warpbreaks and insurance-claims
  data: Poisson or negative binomial, rate ratios, marginal rates,
  exposure offsets, groups with no events and frequency weights.

- [Any GLM family: analysis of deviance with
  anova_glm()](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/glm.md):

  A walkthrough of anova_glm(): a two-way Gaussian ANOVA with Type II
  and Type III tests, and a Gamma model with a log link for a positive,
  right-skewed response, with its coefficient table, dispersion, ratios
  of means and robust standard errors.

### Guides

Topics that cut across the functions.

- [Working with results: the anovakit_fit
  object](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/results.md):

  What every function returns, how to print, extract and reuse it, how
  to go further with emmeans and the fitted model, and how to report a
  result.

- [Diagnostics: what anovakit checks and what to do about
  it](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/diagnostics.md):

  Every assumption check the eight functions run, organised by what is
  being checked: how to read each one, a worked example that makes it
  fire, and the argument or function that helps when it fails. Also
  covers exact fits and the limits of numerical precision.

- [Plots and
  themes](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/visuals.md):

  Every ggplot2 figure the eight functions build, grouped by kind, with
  what to look for in each; then how to change them, set a theme for all
  of them, build your own from the result tables, combine and save them.

- [Weights and robust standard
  errors](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/weights.md):

  How anova_bin(), anova_count() and anova_glm() read prior weights as
  frequencies, trials or sampling weights, what happens to zero weights,
  and where vcov_type’s robust covariance reaches and when it is not
  used.

- [Design
  choices](https://elkronos.github.io/anovakit/articles/design.md):

  Why the defaults are what they are, which decisions a function makes
  for you and where it records them, and which settings can and cannot
  change a result.
